ui.text: IDEA FORGE
EACH STRIKE HAMMERS OUT ONE GAME IDEA BUILT AROUND A SINGLE STRANGE MECHANIC.
A STORY COMES WITH IT UNLESS YOU SWITCH IT OFF.
NO IDEA REPEATS: THE FORGE WALKS EVERY COMBINATION EXACTLY ONCE.
PRESS SPACE TO STRIKE

YOU
you stretch a rope between two drifting anchors and play it like a
slingshot,
you sing notes whose loudness physically shoves everything nearby,
you fold the level like paper along lines you draw with your
finger,
you swap bodies with whatever you point at for as long as you hold
your breath,
you freeze one object in time at a time; freezing a second thaws
the first,
you dig tunnels that only your followers can see or use,
you pour paint; each color changes the physics of whatever it
soaks,
you throw your shadow ahead of you and then become it,
you stack tiny planets and let their combined gravity do the rest,
you tune a radio dial where every frequency rewrites one rule of
the room,
you draw a loop on the ground; everything inside replays its last
five seconds,
you grow vines from your fingertips toward whichever light you
carry,
you whistle to call echoes that copy your last move a beat later,
you pinch the camera to shrink or enlarge the room while you stay
the same size,
you hand every creature a single instruction card that it obeys far
too literally,
you lend your weight to a scale that balances two separate worlds,
you mark things with chalk; whatever is chalked breaks next,
you rotate the entire level a quarter turn while gravity stays
exactly where it is,
you carry the only lantern; nothing exists outside its glow,
you juggle three timers; each one runs a different law of the room,
you tie knots in the path behind you so pursuers tangle in them,
you pluck strings between walls to launch yourself like an arrow,
you spend memories to buy skills; you can hold only three at once,
you conduct a crowd of tiny followers with the tempo of a baton,
you write one word on a wall and the wall starts behaving like that
word,
you pour yourself into containers and flow through the level as
liquid, gas or ice,
you trade places with your own reflection in any mirror, window or
puddle,
you wear a single magnet and flip its polarity to push or pull the
world,
you lay down track one piece at a time while a runaway cart gains
on you,
you cut the level along any straight line and slide the two halves
apart,
you plant seeds that grow into whatever object you were holding
when you planted them,
you keep a pet storm on a leash and aim its lightning with your
footsteps,
BUT
but every object you touch gets a little heavier for the rest of
the level.
but the left half of the world runs at half speed.
but a ghost repeats everything you do exactly one beat late.
but walls are solid only while you are looking at them.
but you can never touch the same surface twice in a row.
but gravity points toward the last thing you touched.
but the level shrinks every time you succeed.
but tools never break; they wear down into different tools.
but everything mirrors itself the moment you stand still.
but silence is solid and noise is a doorway.
but numbers painted on things are real; a 7 weighs seven times a 1.
but the floor gives way on your third visit to any tile.
but you can only move while a partner you do not control moves.
but your color is a rule; only matching things help or hurt you; it
changes with each item you carry.
but time passes only when you change direction.
but thrown objects remember where they came from and return when
thrown again.
but light bends around the biggest thing on screen.
but the exit drifts toward whatever you ignore the longest.
but every move costs a coin and you earn coins only by standing
still.
but a bell rings every ten seconds and you must pick one of three
new laws.
but friend and foe swap sides whenever you cross the midline.
but the more you carry the smaller you become.
but shadows are separate objects that can be picked up.
but speed is shared; whatever you speed up slows something else
down.
but you may only ever turn left.
but anything you stop looking at falls asleep and stays that way.
but each new room is built from your last three mistakes.
but your inventory is physical and trails behind you like a tail.
but up is whichever way you last fell.
but everything you create vanishes the moment you create something
new.
but enemies learn your habits and politely imitate them.
but the world is drawn only by the sounds you make.
PUSHBACK
A slow tide of ink rises from below and erases whatever it touches.
A rival copy of you plays the same level one step ahead and spoils
your route.
The level crumbles from the edges toward the center on a visible
countdown.
A hungry crowd follows you and eats anything you leave unattended.
A storm front sweeps across the map and scatters your tools if it
catches them.
Every ten seconds the room swaps its rules with the room next door.
A quiet creature mirrors your mistakes back at you with interest.
Your energy drains faster the more you succeed.
A wall closes in from one side; each push back costs something you
cannot get again.
Echoes of your earlier attempts haunt the level and block your old
routes.
Gravity grows stronger with every item you collect.
A flock of thieves steals whatever you set down.
A clock-faced beast eats a minute of your day each time it catches
you.
The map builds itself one screen ahead of you while one screen
behind decays.
Noise draws a patient listener that always arrives from a new
direction.
An unseen second player is solving the same puzzle and moves things
behind your back.
Every success wakes something bigger.
Fog rolls in and everything you have not touched recently is
forgotten.
A pendulum of light sweeps the level and scorches anything standing
still.
Your tools multiply when unused and swarm you if you hoard them.
The ground is a slow conveyor and the whole level drifts to the
left.
You carry a fragile guest who panics at sudden moves.
A debt grows every second; only risky moves pay it down.
A tide of rival ghosts races you to claim the same objects.
GOAL
Reach the exit still holding something you started with.
Light every lamp without ever lighting two in neighboring rooms.
Return a lost creature to the place where it first appeared.
Build one unbroken chain from one end of the world to the other.
Empty the level until nothing is left but you.
Balance everything: finish with exactly the same amount on both
sides.
Survive until the final bell while doing as little as possible.
Gather five parts of a machine and assemble them in the right
order.
Teach a stubborn crowd one dance step.
Escape through a door that exists only once you stop searching for
it.
Reach the highest point without ever going down.
Draw a picture with your path that a stranger would recognize.
Put every enemy to sleep at the same moment.
Carry a sleeping friend through ten rooms without waking them.
Give each of your tools to the right person before the level ends.
Grow one thing to full size before anything else around it can.
Leave the level exactly as you found it.
Reach a stranger on the far side who has the very same problem.
Finish with the fewest actions; the quietest run scores highest.
Win a round by deliberately losing the round before it.
Fill the whole map with color.
Teach your pursuer to stop chasing.
Make the loudest sound the level is able to make.
Be the last thing standing in a world that shrinks to a point.
STORY
A retired lighthouse keeper in a harbor town that is slowly
floating away.
A courier in a city whose streets rearrange themselves every night.
The last apprentice of a clockmaker who stopped time and then
vanished.
A stray cat that the whole neighborhood believes is a small god.
A cartographer mapping a country that dislikes being mapped.
A night nurse at a hospital that treats broken machines.
A kite maker whose kites carry messages between rival mountains.
A ghost who must finish one chore before the house can be sold.
A deep sea diver who keeps finding rooms that were built for her.
A baker whose bread remembers whoever eats it.
A traveling choir with one voice missing and a long road ahead.
A robot gardener tending a park for people who have all left.
A student whose homework turns into the place they must walk
through.
A pair of twins who share one pair of hands.
A beekeeper on a space station with no flowers.
A forgotten statue that gets exactly one night each year to move.
A sailor on a ship that sails across the sky at low tide.
A mail carrier delivering letters addressed to people who do not
exist yet.
A tiny dragon applying for a very ordinary job.
A librarian guarding a book that rewrites whoever reads it.
A thief who must return everything they ever stole, one night at a
time.
A lamplighter in a town where the dark is alive and rather shy.
A grandmother driving a very slow, very important truck.
A tour guide leading visitors through a city that exists only while
it is being described.
STORY OFF. JUST THE MECHANIC.
